html-i01-semantic-layout.q: You are marking up a blog post teaser that will also appear in the site's RSS feed and on a category page. Which wrapper is correct?
options: <section>, because it is a section of the listing page
<article>, because the teaser is self-contained and makes sense republished elsewhere
<aside>, because teasers are secondary content
<main>, because the teaser is the important content of the card
html-i01-semantic-layout.why: The syndication test decides it: content that still makes sense distributed on its own — feed entries, posts, cards — is an article, regardless of where it currently appears.

html-i01-semantic-layout.q: A template accidentally renders two <main> elements: one around the page content and one inside the article. What is the correct fix?
options: Keep both — HTML allows any number of main elements
Keep the inner one and delete the outer one
Keep the single outer main for the page's unique content and change the inner one to article or a div
Replace both with <section> to avoid the conflict
html-i01-semantic-layout.why: A page gets exactly one main, wrapping its unique content; anything nested inside an article that needs grouping is a job for article internals, section or a plain div.

html-i01-semantic-layout.q: You want the post's title and publish date grouped at the top of the article, while the site logo and menu sit at the top of the page. What markup expresses both?
options: Two <header> elements: one inside body for the site, one inside the article for the post
One <header> only — a second header element is invalid
A <header> for the site and a <nav> for the post title
A <section> for the site banner and a <header> for the post
html-i01-semantic-layout.why: header attaches to its nearest ancestor, so a page-level header and an article-level header coexist correctly — each introduces its own container.

html-i02-why-semantics.q: A screen-reader user complains they must listen through your entire menu on every page before reaching the content. Which change fixes the root cause?
options: Add more descriptive class names like class="main-content"
Wrap the unique content in <main> so it becomes a jumpable landmark
Move the menu below the content in the source
Reduce the number of menu items
html-i02-why-semantics.why: Landmarks come from semantic elements, not class names — a real <main> lets screen-reader users jump straight past the repeated chrome with one keystroke.

html-i02-why-semantics.q: During a refactor you meet <div class="card-wrapper"> whose only purpose is to carry the card's border and shadow styles. What should you do?
options: Convert it to <section> — every div should become semantic
Convert it to <article> since it wraps a card
Leave it as a div — purely presentational grouping is exactly what div is for
Delete it and move the styles to body
html-i02-why-semantics.why: Semantic markup means choosing meaningful elements where meaning exists; a styling-only wrapper has none, so div is the correct, honest choice.

html-i02-why-semantics.q: Inside <main><article>...</article></main> on a page whose h1 is the site title, what level should the article's title heading be?
options: h1 — each article restarts the outline at h1
h2 — the document has one outline and the article title sits one level under the page h1
h3 — one level per wrapper element (main, then article)
Any level, because sectioning elements renumber headings automatically
html-i02-why-semantics.why: The HTML5 outline algorithm was never implemented and is gone from the standard: heading levels are numbered explicitly across the whole document, so a title directly under the h1 is an h2.

html-i03-tables-basics.q: Your rendered table shows a gap: the third row is missing its last cell. What is the most likely cause?
options: The table element is missing a columns attribute
That tr contains fewer cells than the other rows
A th was used where a td belongs
The table needs border-collapse in CSS
html-i03-tables-basics.why: HTML tables are row-major and every row must supply the same number of cell positions; a short row leaves a visible hole in the grid.

html-i03-tables-basics.q: In a nutrition table each row starts with the nutrient name (Protein, Fat, Sugar) labelling the numbers to its right. How should those first cells be marked up?
options: <td> with bold styling so they stand out
<th scope="col"> because they are in the first column
<th scope="row"> because each labels the cells of its own row
<caption> elements, one per row
html-i03-tables-basics.why: They are header cells for their rows, so th with scope="row" — scope describes the direction a header applies, not where the cell happens to sit.

html-i03-tables-basics.q: A colleague proposes using a table to place the sidebar next to the article, 'like the old days'. What is the right assessment?
options: Fine — tables render reliably in every browser
Wrong tool: layout belongs to CSS, and a layout table is announced to screen readers as data that is not there
Acceptable if every cell gets scope attributes
Only wrong if the table has visible borders
html-i03-tables-basics.why: Tables assert 'this is tabular data' to every consumer of the page; using one for positioning misleads assistive technology and forfeits the better CSS layout tools.

html-i04-tables-structure.q: A 30-page expense report prints with column labels visible only on page one. Which markup change fixes the printout?
options: Move the header row into a <thead>, which browsers repeat on every printed page
Add a <caption> above the table
Duplicate the header row every 40 data rows
Set scope="col" on the header cells
html-i04-tables-structure.why: Print engines repeat thead rows at the top of each page of a split table — but only if the rows are actually grouped in a thead.

html-i04-tables-structure.q: You want the whole 'Amount' column shaded without touching every cell. Where can that styling hook live in the markup?
options: On the tr elements, since they contain the cells
On a <col> inside <colgroup> positioned to cover that column
On the tfoot element
Nowhere — columns cannot be addressed in HTML at all
html-i04-tables-structure.why: colgroup/col exist precisely to describe columns in row-major markup; a col accepts background, width, border and visibility, so a background shade hangs on it cleanly.

html-i04-tables-structure.q: document.querySelector('table > tr') returns null even though your table clearly has rows written directly inside it. Why?
options: querySelector cannot traverse into tables
The parser wrapped your bare rows in an implicit tbody, so no tr is a direct child of table
Rows only match selectors when a thead exists
The > combinator is invalid for table elements
html-i04-tables-structure.why: Browsers auto-insert tbody around stray rows during parsing; writing tbody explicitly keeps the source truthful and your selectors predictable.

html-i05-tables-spanning.q: You add rowspan="3" to a category cell, and now each of the next two rows shows a cell jutting past the table's right edge. What went wrong?
options: rowspan values above 2 are invalid
The next two rows still contain a cell for that column, whose position the rowspan already reserved
The table is missing a colgroup
rowspan must also be declared on the table element
html-i05-tables-spanning.why: A rowspan pre-claims the same column position in following rows, so those rows must omit that cell — supplying it anyway pushes every cell rightward and overhangs the grid.

html-i05-tables-spanning.q: A 'Contact details' header spans the Phone and Email columns. Which scope value does it take?
options: scope="col" — it is in the header row
scope="row" — it spans horizontally
scope="colgroup" — it labels a group of columns
No scope — spanned headers cannot take one
html-i05-tables-spanning.why: A header covering several columns describes the group, not a single column, so colgroup is the correct scope (rowgroup being the vertical mirror).

html-i05-tables-spanning.q: A table's header geometry is too irregular for scope to describe which headers apply to which cells. What is the standard HTML mechanism to keep it accessible?
options: Give each header an id and list the applicable ids in each data cell's headers attribute
Add aria-label to the table element summarising the layout
Repeat the header text inside every data cell
Wrap each irregular block in its own tfoot
html-i05-tables-spanning.why: The headers/id technique wires every data cell to its headers explicitly, covering relationships scope cannot express — at the cost of maintaining the id lists truthfully.

html-i06-forms-basics.q: A login form was built with method="get" and now passwords appear in the server's access logs. Why, and what is the fix?
options: GET encrypts weakly; switch the site to HTTPS and keep GET
GET puts the data in the URL, which servers log; switch the form to method="post" so it travels in the request body
The name attributes leaked; rename the fields
The action URL was absolute; make it relative
html-i06-forms-basics.why: GET serialises all pairs into the query string — visible in history, logs and shared links — so credentials and any private data must travel by POST.

html-i06-forms-basics.q: A user fills in a styled input and submits, but the server never receives that field at all. The input has an id, a label and a placeholder. What is missing?
options: A value attribute
The required attribute
The name attribute — without it the browser skips the control entirely when building the submission
An enctype on the form
html-i06-forms-basics.why: Only named controls contribute name=value pairs; id serves the page internally, but the server keys everything off name.

html-i06-forms-basics.q: Your product filter form should produce results users can bookmark and share with colleagues. Which method fits and why?
options: POST, because filters may contain several values
GET, because the parameters become part of the URL, making the result page bookmarkable and shareable
POST, because GET forms cannot have submit buttons
Either — method only affects encoding speed
html-i06-forms-basics.why: GET's defining property is that the submission is the URL: reloading or sharing it reproduces the same read-only query, exactly right for searches and filters.

html-i07-labels-inputs.q: Clicking the 'Email' text does nothing, though the markup has <label for="email"> and an input with name="email". What is wrong?
options: The label must come after the input in the source
for pairs with the input's id, not its name — the input needs id="email"
Labels only work inside fieldsets
The input needs a placeholder to activate the label
html-i07-labels-inputs.why: The pairing contract is for ↔ id, exactly matched; a name attribute plays no part, and a dangling for fails silently.

html-i07-labels-inputs.q: A designer wants minimal forms: no visible labels, just grey hint text inside each field. What is the professional objection?
options: Grey text renders differently across browsers
The hint disappears once typing starts, may not be announced by assistive tech, and typically fails contrast — placeholder cannot be the only label
Placeholders slow down form submission
Hints inside fields prevent autofill entirely
html-i07-labels-inputs.why: placeholder is an optional format hint, not a field name; if the design demands the look, a real label restyled with CSS keeps accessibility intact.

html-i07-labels-inputs.q: Adding a <button> that toggles password visibility suddenly makes the login form submit whenever it is clicked. Why?
options: Buttons may not contain icons
Inside a form, a button without an explicit type defaults to type="submit"
JavaScript click handlers always trigger submission
The button must be moved outside the form to work
html-i07-labels-inputs.why: The default type of button inside a form is submit — every script-only button needs an explicit type="button" to stay inert.

html-i08-input-types-choice.q: Users can somehow select Small, Medium and Large simultaneously in your size chooser built from three radio inputs. What is the bug?
options: Radios need JavaScript to enforce exclusivity
The three radios have different name attributes, so each is its own group of one
The checked attribute is missing
Radios must live inside a select element
html-i08-input-types-choice.why: Radio exclusivity comes solely from a shared name within the form; differing names create independent groups that can all be active at once.

html-i08-input-types-choice.q: The server receives size=on instead of the chosen size. Which attribute was forgotten on the radio inputs?
options: value — without it a selected control submits the literal default 'on'
id — the server cannot resolve the element
label — unlabeled controls submit placeholders
checked — unchecked groups send 'on'
html-i08-input-types-choice.why: The submitted pair is name=value; with no value attribute the browser falls back to 'on', which tells the server that something was picked but not what.

html-i08-input-types-choice.q: A screen-reader user hears 'Medium, radio button' but has no idea what question Medium answers. What markup provides that context?
options: A heading element directly above the radios
A title attribute on each input
A fieldset around the group with a legend stating the question, announced together with each option
Longer label text on every option
html-i08-input-types-choice.why: legend is the programmatic name of the group: assistive technology announces it with each option's label, turning 'Medium' into 'Size, Medium'.

html-i09-input-types-modern.q: Users typing Greek postal codes report that '01234' becomes '1234' and the field shows spinner arrows. What went wrong in the markup?
options: The maxlength attribute is missing
type="number" was used for digit-like data that is not a quantity — leading zeros vanish; use text or tel with validation
The min attribute defaults to 1
Postal codes require type="search"
html-i09-input-types-modern.why: number treats input as a mathematical value, normalising away leading zeros and offering steppers; codes and ids are digit strings, not numbers.

html-i09-input-types-modern.q: With min="0", max="10" and step="2" on a number input, a user types 7 and the form refuses to submit. Why?
options: 7 exceeds the permitted number of characters
Steps count from min, so only even values are on the validity grid — 7 falls between steps
max must be a multiple of step
Typed values bypass validation; only spinner values are checked
html-i09-input-types-modern.why: step defines a grid anchored at min (0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 here); values off the grid are invalid even when inside the range — use step="any" to allow all.

html-i09-input-types-modern.q: A checkout page stores the price in <input type="hidden" name="price" value="49.90"> and charges whatever comes back. What is the security assessment?
options: Safe — hidden inputs cannot be seen or edited by users
Safe if the form uses POST
Vulnerable — hidden means not rendered, not protected; anyone can change the value, so the server must derive the price itself
Vulnerable only over HTTP, safe over HTTPS
html-i09-input-types-modern.why: Hidden fields are plainly editable in DevTools or a crafted request; they may carry identifiers to look up, never values the server trusts blindly.

html-i10-input-types-datetime.q: You preset a date field with value="20/08/2026" and the field renders empty. What is the rule you violated?
options: value cannot be preset on date inputs
The wire format is always ISO YYYY-MM-DD regardless of locale — value="2026-08-20" is required
Dates must be set via the min attribute
The slash separator needs URL-encoding
html-i10-input-types-datetime.why: Display is localised but the machine format is fixed: value, min, max and the submitted data all use YYYY-MM-DD, so non-ISO strings are simply ignored.

html-i10-input-types-datetime.q: A global webinar signup uses <input type="datetime-local"> alone, and attendees from other timezones join an hour off. Why?
options: datetime-local rounds to the nearest hour
The value deliberately carries no timezone — the server needs the user's zone captured separately to compute the true instant
The T separator corrupts the value in transit
Browsers convert the value to UTC inconsistently
html-i10-input-types-datetime.why: datetime-local means 'this wall-clock time, zone unspecified' — perfect for local appointments, insufficient for global instants without a separately captured timezone.

html-i10-input-types-datetime.q: In a browser without month-input support, <input type="month"> renders as a plain text box. What keeps the form usable there?
options: Nothing — the form cannot submit in that browser
The browser downloads a picker automatically
The field still submits as text, so document the YYYY-MM format near the label and validate format and range on the server
Adding required forces the browser to render a picker
html-i10-input-types-datetime.why: Unknown types degrade to text inputs that still submit under their name; visible format hints plus server-side validation make the degraded path safe.
